ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A poor child remembering old debts is someone with little present capital still occupied by liabilities carried from before.
EvidenceBody: Dabo Qian makes the phrase a direct answer about the meaning of the western arrival. Chijue Daochong comments with it when an attendant cannot return the rhinoceros fan; Wufeng Ruxue uses it in answer to why Shakyamuni appeared. Tianyin Yuanxiu and Poshan Haiming apply it critically to belated review of old errors or reverence for earlier masters. The Zen bend makes remembered debt a figure for being pulled back into inherited accounts precisely when a present response is required.
